prediction.likelyOutcome: This is a genuine jury question on a single controlling fact issue — whether the ~$500,000 Petco Site-Specific Work fell inside or outside the GMP Contract — with Brexton holding real, testimony-backed support for its position but facing a serious lien-waiver obstacle to the foreclosure remedy specifically. Four Elyria's fraud and slander-of-title counts are comparatively weak derivative theories unlikely to survive dispositive motions or trial given the good-faith nature of the scope dispute. Net, Brexton is more likely than not to recover a meaningful share of the Site-Specific Work claim via breach of contract or unjust enrichment, even if the lien itself is partly or wholly extinguished by the unconditional waivers.

outcome.description: The trial court held the Site-Specific Work was outside the contract, granted summary judgment against Four Elyria on all its claims and for Brexton on unjust enrichment, and after a damages-only jury trial entered judgment for Brexton for $465,417.44; both sides' attorney-fee motions were denied and Brexton's lien-foreclosure counterclaim was dismissed. On this second appeal the court of appeals agreed the work was outside the contract but reversed in part and remanded for the trial court to apply the contract's Article 9 change-order provisions, leaving the unjust-enrichment award and the fee issues to be revisited on remand.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed in part and remanded; no final figure yet.
